textRuns.value: INSIGHT:
Unplanned admission rates show
substantial dispersion across facilities
, with values spanning a wide range relative to their
own peer-group median benchmarks
. Facilities appear on both sides of their peer medians across all peer groups, indicating that elevated unplanned intake is
not confined to a single facility type or segment
The distribution highlights
within–peer-group variability
, where some facilities operate materially above their peer median while others fall below, even under similar structural classifications. This pattern reflects
heterogeneous intake exposure within shared peer contexts
, rather than uniform pressure across all facilities in a group.
Importantly, the peer median line functions as a
directional reference
, not a threshold. Positions above or below this line indicate relative intake alignment within peer context, not performance standing.
INTERPRETATION GUIDANCE:
Interpret this visual as a
within–peer-group positioning view
, showing how facilities’ unplanned intake rates align relative to their
own peer medians
, not as a cross-facility comparison.
Variation above or below the peer median should be read as
differences in intake exposure and demand patterns
, not evidence of better or worse operational performance.
Facilities above their peer median may be operating under
greater structural intake pressure
, while those below may experience comparatively lower unplanned demand — both conditions can exist simultaneously within the same peer group.
This view should be used to
contextualize downstream metrics
(e.g., LOS, cost, throughput) by highlighting differences in intake conditions that persist even among structurally similar facilities.
Avoid using this visual to infer causality, effectiveness of intake management, or quality of care. The chart provides
contextual alignment
, not evaluative judgment.
